    concepts each of the first three weeks assumes, with links to pre-recorded

    [2024/25](/ilias-2024-25/mk68-00-part-1-prerequisites.pdf) and

## Key handbooks

This is the content of the additional literature sheet distributed to the
2024/25 cohort
([mk68-additional-literature.pdf](/ilias-2024-25/mk68-additional-literature.pdf)).

**Statistics**

-   📖 **OpenIntro Statistics**, David Diez, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and
    Christopher Barr, 2019. [openintro.org/book/os](https://www.openintro.org/book/os/)
    (free PDF). The chapters used:
    -   1.3 Sampling principles and strategies
    -   1.4 Experiments
    -   Chapter 2 Summarizing data
    -   3.1 Defining probability, in particular 3.1.2 Law of large numbers
    -   3.4 Random variables
    -   3.5 Continuous distributions
    -   4.1 Normal distribution
    -   Chapter 7 Inference for numerical data
    -   Chapter 8 Introduction to linear regression

**Econometrics**

-   📖 **Mastering 'Metrics: the path from cause to effect**, Joshua D. Angrist
    and Jörn-Steffen Pischke, Princeton University Press, 2015.
    [Find it in the JLU library](https://justfind.hds.hebis.de/Record/HEB35797798X).
    Only:
    -   Chapter 1 Randomized Trials
    -   Chapter 2 Regression

**Notable additions**

-   📖 **Fundamentals of Data Visualization**, Claus O. Wilke, 2019, at
    [clauswilke.com/dataviz](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz): more about
    visualising distributions. Pay attention to Part I, From data to
    visualization, Chapters 6 to 9.
-   📖 More on income and inequality from Our World in Data:
    [What is the Gini coefficient](https://ourworldindata.org/what-is-the-gini-coefficient)
    and
    [the history of global economic inequality](https://ourworldindata.org/the-history-of-global-economic-inequality).
